_about: Exchange templates as data (Combat). Two timing profiles per branch. 'parity' reproduces sim/director/melee.gd, beam.gd and exchange.gd chain() at commit 69c4a2f exactly: same beats, same scheduling order, same RNG draws in the same order. 'spaced' keeps every outcome, damage, force, tag and draw of parity but re-times the beats to balance-targets.md section 10 (0.25 to 0.40 s between contacts, 6 to 10 beats) and adds render-only 'cue' beats. Contract, value forms and verification: docs/combat/data-fields.md section 10 and docs/combat/s3b-loader-note.md.

approach._note: rt = clamp(dist / divisor, min, max), melee.gd line 19

tempo._note: ticks. step 0.35 s between contacts; windup 0.25 s before a parryable strike (proposal for Controls, section 10 asks 0.20 to 0.30); heavyWindup 0.333 s (Controls' 20-tick proposal); follow 0.05 s from a strike to its launch; tell 0.30 s. QA tunes 'step' first: each +3 ticks moves the median exchange by about +0.2 s

approach.rounding: round half up to whole ticks
approach._note: c (the contact anchor) = clamp(dist / divisor, min, max) seconds for dist up to 'beyond'; past it a visible pursuit flight of clamp(base + (dist - beyond) / per, base, max) s (section 10: 0.8 to 2.0 s). Encounter applies SimConst.WS as it does today

spaced._aiNote: The AI defender's press delay after the wind beat. With the wider 0.25 s window, [0.05, 0.54] keeps the AI's parry success per attempt near today's 41%. Encounter owns the AI policy and may retune.

parry._note: Widths, buffer and hit-stop ticks are Controls' (docs/controls/rulings.md sections 3 and 5). Combat accepts the clean-parry reward: +4 ki (12 in all), a 12-tick freeze and a distinct cue, with no extra damage, so the parry stays a tempo and resource reward rather than a damage source. Parity keeps the code's values (18 damage, 8 ki, stop 0.12 s, pushback 520).

hitstopFloors._note: section 10 floors, a proposal for Controls (hit-stop table owner). The loader applies max(stop, floor) only once Controls adopts them

tempo._note: ticks. step 0.233 s between contacts (Orb's feel over section 10's 0.25 to 0.40; the prototype ran 0.16 to 0.20). windup and heavyWindup are Controls' rulings (15 and 20). foot 0.15 s is a footwork move (backstep, pivot, circle). pursue 0.35 s is the attacker (or the winning defender) chasing a launched body through the chain window. No beat is a still hold: every cue shares its tick with a motion or a contact. enderWindup 0.3 s is the wind-up of a string's last blow (Game Design: 18 ticks, with a perfect-block window). stepIn 0.1 s is the step that closes a striker to contact distance, ending on the contact tick. chainClose 0.2 s is the chain link's catch, which now ends on its strike. stepAround 0.133 s is the evasive defender's step-around (the dodge beat with side 'cross'): over the attacker and down behind it. Keep it at 9 ticks or under (three follows), because DODGE & COUNTER's step-in starts then.

approach.rounding: round half up to whole ticks
approach._note: min 0.25 s (15 ticks) so the light wind-up always falls inside the approach flight: the attacker is visibly closing while the parry window is open.
approach._minHeavy: seconds; 20 ticks. A heavy exchange approaches in at least this, so the heavy opener's 20-tick wind-up fits inside the flight (min stays for lights).

dynamic._aiNote: as spaced: keeps the AI's parry success per attempt near 41% with the 15-tick window. Encounter owns it.

parry._note: Widths, buffer and hit-stop ticks are Controls' (docs/controls/rulings.md sections 3 and 5). Combat accepts the clean-parry reward: +4 ki (12 in all), a 12-tick freeze and a distinct cue, with no extra damage, so the parry stays a tempo and resource reward rather than a damage source. Parity keeps the code's values (18 damage, 8 ki, stop 0.12 s, pushback 520).
parry._retire: Leaves with Encounter's step 3 (the perfect block replaces the parry and Game Design withdrew the clean parry). Kept in 2b so behaviour does not change early.

hitstopFloors._note: section 10 floors, a proposal for Controls (hit-stop table owner). The loader applies max(stop, floor) only once Controls adopts them

windups._note: ticks of visible wind-up by strike class (moveset-system.md section 9.7; control-rules.md section 1). opener, heavy, ender and blast carry a perfect-block window in their last perfectBlock.windowTicks; mid and none have none.

perfectBlock._note: Game Design's numbers (control-rules.md section 1). Read from Encounter's step 3; until then the 'parry' block and the wind beats run as today.

strikeClass._rule2b: In the dynamic profile a strike's o.class replaces o.noParry. Until step 3 wires per-strike windows, a strike can be parried only when its class is opener, heavy or ender AND it is the attacker's first strike after a wind beat. That reproduces today's dynamic behaviour exactly: the parryable strikes are the openers of TRADE BLOWS, PRESSURE and GUARD BREAK and HEAVY CLASH - WON's deciding blow.

contact._note: units (u), centre to centre. Animation measured that a hand, the hips' lunge and a step-in reach about 68 u at the same height (pose-pipeline.md section 9.3). Every damaging strike must find the two fighters within 'reach' and at the same height on its contact tick: the approach, lunge or step-in before it ends at 'offset'. minSeparation is the least distance two bodies may come (no overlap). Sides: an offset is measured on the mover's own side of its target, never from its facing; only a beat with args.side 'cross' may change sides, and each branch states where the pair ends in 'endSides'.
contact._placement: placementReaches: a damaging strike places its striker at 'offset', on its own side and at the target's height, when the target is within this many reaches (3 x 68 = 204 u; the sim adds two ticks of the target's flight, which stays in code). Past it nothing moves and the feed says OUT OF REACH.
contact._stepAround: While teleporting is on hold, the dodge beat with side 'cross' is a step-around, not a blink. args.dur is its length (tempo.stepAround). args.rise is how far above the attacker it passes (98 u, about 1.3 body heights; it passes under the attacker at the flight ceiling). args.off is the distance behind the attacker where it ends, at the attacker's height (74 u: outside 'reach' on purpose, so the next strike needs its own step-in or turn). No draw.
contact._lead: Announce rule (Animation needs 6 ticks to wind a blow up): every strike beat is scheduled when its exchange, chain link or finisher is planned, never on the tick it lands. The shortest lead in this file is 12 ticks (the chain link: tempo.chainClose); an exchange's first strike comes at least approach.min (15 ticks) after the plan. Keep tempo.chainClose and approach.min at 6 ticks or more. A strike beat that comes due after a parry deals nothing (the exchange is cancelled) and must not be drawn as a blow: contact-spacing.md section 7.

locals.rt: approach(dist) in the active profile: 'rt' in parity (seconds), 'c' in spaced (ticks)

interrupts._about: Branch takeovers that arrive inside an exchange (docs/combat/control-scheme-data.md section 4; Encounter's control-scheme-plan.md). The director drops the branch's pending beats and schedules the interrupt's beats from that tick. A branch lists the ones it allows in 'interrupts'; dodge_cancel and burst apply to every branch by control-rules.md section 2. Same-tick precedence: perfect_block, reversal, dodge_cancel, burst, the defender before the attacker. Read from Encounter's step 3; step 2b only carries the data.

perfect_block._note: the attacker's string ends and it staggers; the defender keeps its momentum. A perfect block of a blast deflects it; of a signature, see beam.outcomeByProfile

reversal.then: the defender's own exchange starts (a throw or a sweep), with the roles swapped
reversal._note: 20 ki, or 10 after 2 s of continuous guard; 6 s cooldown (Game Design)

dodge_cancel._note: Encounter's step 3: 12 ticks of invulnerability and a dash in the held direction; the exchange ends with no winner. 15 ki, 3 s cooldown

burst._note: Encounter's step 3: the defender's answer under pressure; 30 ki and a cooldown. A guarding rival absorbs it and the burster staggers 30 ticks

selector._formula: pEsc = clamp(0.5 + 0.07*(D.tier - A.tier) + (dist > 800 ? 0.12 : 0) - (A.ambush ? 1 : 0), 0.05, 0.88); one S.rng.next(), drawn before any beat is scheduled (melee.gd lines 33-34)

branches._spacedNote: An escape is short by design (5 beats): holding the attacker longer would be dead air.

selector._formula: pRead = A.ambush ? 1.0 : clamp(0.42 + 0.08*(A.tier - D.tier) + (A.stance == 0 ? 0.08 : 0) - (A.ki < 12 ? 0.12 : 0) - (heavy ? 0.05 : 0), 0.15, 0.8); one S.rng.next(), always drawn, even under an ambush (melee.gd lines 51-52)

branches._spacedNote: The parity wind beat (a parry window that can never parry, CC-009) is dropped in spaced; that removes the AI defender's press draws here.

branches._note: stance-matrix.md section 7.2: not read, and the defender asked for no counter. The dodge succeeds and nobody is hit.

dynamic._formula: the read roll is unchanged (one S.rng.next(), always drawn). Not read: DODGE & COUNTER only when the defender has its own attack queued (defQueued, from Encounter), otherwise DODGE - CLEAN (stance-matrix.md section 7.2)

selector._formula: counter if D.ki > 25 and S.rng.next() < 0.4. The draw happens only when the gate passes (short-circuit), after the three strikes are scheduled (melee.gd line 74)

branches._ruleNote: Game Design's R6 (no chain window after GUARD HOLDS) is a rule change for a later slice; both profiles keep today's window.

dynamic._formula: R4 re-ruled (stance-matrix.md section 7.3): a held guard never counters by itself, so there is no roll. The counter comes from the perfect_block interrupt (then the riposte) or the reversal interrupt

selector._formula: won if score(A, D) > score(D, A), score(f, o) = f.tier + f.ki / 70 + S.rng.range_(0, 1.6) + (vitality(f) > vitality(o) ? 0.3 : 0), summed left to right; A's score (and its draw) first (melee.gd lines 94 and 129-130)

dynamic._formula: as 'selector', plus the retreat entry: defenderAdd is added to the defender's score after its sum (about +15 points of win chance against a rush, stance-matrix.md section 7.2). No extra draw

templates._trigger2b: AGGRESSIVE is Press: the defender has its own attack request (defQueued). A defender holding nothing is NEUTRAL and gets clean_hit or clean_hit_heavy (stance-matrix.md section 7.1).

selector._formula: p = clamp(0.5 + 0.09*(A.tier - D.tier) + (A.ki > D.ki ? 0.05 : -0.05), 0.2, 0.8); r = S.rng.next(); won if r < p - 0.12, countered if r > p + 0.12, else shockwave (melee.gd lines 109-125)

templates._spacedNote: In spaced the wind beat belongs to WON only: COUNTERED and SHOCKWAVE have no parryable strike, so a wind there would be a silent dead window that also costs an AI draw (Controls' rulings, section 2). Parity keeps the shared wind, as the code does.

dynamic._formula: as 'selector', plus the retreat entry: a defender who pressed while holding away, against a rush, takes 0.10 off the attacker's p (stance-matrix.md section 7.2). defEntry and atkEntry are -1, 0 or +1, from Encounter; 0 until entries are wired

templates._trigger2b: AGGRESSIVE is Press: the defender has its own attack request (defQueued). A defender holding nothing is NEUTRAL and gets clean_hit or clean_hit_heavy (stance-matrix.md section 7.1).

selector._formula: stance-matrix.md section 7.1: a defender holding nothing is hit. CLIPPED when it was flying at more than half speed across or away (defClipped, from Encounter). No draw

templates._about: control-rules.md section 1: the defender's attack within perfectBlock.riposteTicks of its perfect block. It cannot be blocked or dodged, and it launches when the blocked strike was a heavy or an ender (riposteLaunch, from Encounter). Read from step 3.

chainLink._about: Scheduled by exchange.gd chain() when the attacker presses in an open chain window. Times are relative to the press (t = ex.t). combo++, ext = null, ki -6 and the banner stay in code. chainStrike's damage (52 + 7*combo) stays in the op for S3b.

beam._spacedNote: Identical in the first spaced pass: the beam's follow-on timing (rise 0.55 s, dodge and escape at +0.02, hold +0.9, clash 1.6 s and +2.6 s) lives inside the ops in beam.gd. 'laterSpaced' lists proposed values for when Encounter exposes those constants.

outcome._formula: beam.gd lines 15-23, evaluated in this order

rules._note: the draw is always taken first, then 'and not A.ambush' is tested. A negative coef is exact: a + (-b)*c equals a - b*c bit for bit
kept with today's sign for parity (CC-004; Game Design's R7 fixes it in a later slice)

laterSpaced._note: proposed: non-clash beams 2.4 s, clashes 4.2 s (section 10 set pieces: 3 to 8 s), with a 'focus' cue at 0.65 s

dynamic._about: stance-matrix.md section 7.2 and control-rules.md section 1: the director never fires a beam on its own. The outcome is decided at the fire beat from what the defender did during the tell; the first matching rule wins. The draws below move to that tick. The automatic rule (AGGRESSIVE with 40 ki) is gone from this profile.

rules._note: the defender fired its own signature (45 ki, off cooldown): a full struggle
a heavy energy attack with 40 ki or more: a clash at -10 on the defender's score
a perfect block during the tell (from step 3)
Press without an energy answer, NEUTRAL, or CHARGING: the beam goes through
